title: observability: token-level + KV cost/latency dashboards, tracing enrichment, and alert tuning
author: Priya Raman
release_notes: Adds token-level cost & latency dashboards with KV-cache-aware breakdowns, enriches KV spans for better trace linking, and tunes alert thresholds to reduce noisy SLO alerts. Backwards-compatible; no user-visible API changes.
body:
Motivation: We see noisy SLO alerts and poor triage velocity when investigating tail-latency and KV-cache impact on token cost. This PR adds token-level cost and latency dashboards (including KV cache hit/miss breakdowns), enriches KV spans so traces link to token metrics, and refines alert thresholds and grouping to reduce noise.

What this PR does: 1) New dashboards: token_kv_cost_latency.jsonnet (console) with per-model, per-route breakdowns, 95/99/99.9 latency bands, and token-cost attribution to KV hits/misses. 2) Tracing: span enrichment in serving/telemetry to attach kv.cache_hit and kv.lookup_ms to spans so traces join with metrics dashboards. 3) Metrics: new Prometheus rules for token_kv_alerts.yml and a revised recording rule set to pre-aggregate token-level histograms for fast dashboarding. 4) Alerts: tuned thresholds and grouping (route + model + region) to reduce duplicate notifications and align with SLO burn rates. 5) Tests and examples: e2e observability test, small notebook example, and dashboard component updates in the console.

Design notes: dashboards are authored in jsonnet that composes existing token-level panels; metric names follow the new token_ prefix convention. Tracing enrichment intentionally attaches only low-cardinality kv.{cache_hit,lookup_ms_ms_bucket} tags to avoid high-cardinality explosion. Alert tuning aligns 1h burn + 6h sustained windows and uses grouped_by labels to reduce pager noise.

Rollback plan: revert console/dashboard json and the prometheus rules (two files) which will immediately stop alerting and remove panels. Tracing enrichment is additive; safe to revert if unforeseen cardinality issues occur.

Testing: unit tests for the KV metrics exporter, integration test that validates the enriched spans show kv tags, and e2e test that verifies dashboards render expected panels under synthetic load. CI run is green (see checks below).

Related: ENG-6421 (observability improvements), SRE-128 (alert noise reduction).

review_comments: Lara Chen: Can we confirm the kv tags are low-cardinality? We should avoid adding raw keys like user_id. (requested changes)
Priya Raman: Confirmed \u2014 we only attach kv.cache_hit (true|false) and kv.lookup_ms_bucket (buckets). Added unit tests and a comment in kv_span_enrichment.go to enforce this. (author reply)
Mateo Silva: Alerts look good but suggest grouping by (route, model, region) to avoid duplicates \u2014 applied in token_kv_alerts.yml. (approved)
Jordan Wu: Integration test flaked once on CI; reran and it passed. Consider adding a small retry in the test harness to reduce flakiness. (comment)
Priya Raman: Added a 2s backoff retry to the e2e test and documented it in ci/metrics_tests.yaml. (author reply)
notes_on_backward_compatibility: No API or data format breaking changes. Tracing enrichment adds optional tags only. Dashboards are additive.
changelog_entry: Observability: add token-level cost & latency dashboards with KV cache breakdowns; enrich traces with KV tags; tune alerts to reduce noise (ENG-6421, SRE-128).
user_facing_changes: console: new Token-level KV cost/latency dashboard; no changes to public REST/SDK APIs.
manual_steps: After deploy: 1) apply infra/prometheus/rules/token_kv_alerts.yml to Prometheus, 2) import redwood-console/dashboards/token_kv_cost_latency.jsonnet into the Console, 3) monitor alerts for 24h and revert thresholds if needed.
examples: examples/observability/token-cost-example.ipynb demonstrates dashboard queries and trace linking for a synthetic workload.
